about: A small multi-turn probe for the API's per-thread conversation memory (agent/memory.py). Eight conversations of two or three turns over the five FY2025 10-Ks; every follow-up leaves out something the previous turn supplied (the company, the year, the metric, or a pronoun or ellipsis), so a system with no memory cannot answer it. NOT part of the 71-item benchmark: separate ids, never hashed into benchmark_version, no chunk labels. N is small (11 follow-up turns in 8 conversations): the probe shows that memory works and is worth its design, it does not estimate a rate.
how_to_run: python -m eval.run_multi_turn_probe --label <label>  (see eval/run_multi_turn_probe.py; 30 requests, about $0.075 actual)
ground_truth_provenance: Every figure was read from data/facts.sqlite (the XBRL facts parsed from the filings on disk, python -m ingestion.xbrl) by an SQL query on ticker, concept, fiscal_year and dimension, never from model memory. Each turn lists the facts.id rows it rests on; tests/test_multi_turn_probe.py re-checks every id, ticker, concept, fiscal year and value against the database when it is present. Fiscal years follow the filing's own label: Apple's fiscal 2025 ends 2025-09-27 and Microsoft's ends 2025-06-30, the others end 2025-12-31.
scoring: eval/figure_match.py::figure_match(ground_truth, answer), the judge-free check behind figure_primary: the answer contains the first non-year figure of the ground truth. A refused answer scores as not found.
